newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares boosted by brewery upturn.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares boosted by brewery upturn.

text.p: Nigerian shares maintained their upward trend in Wednesday's session, which saw troubled brewery shares suddenly become attractive, dealers said.
Due to technical problems the all share index was not updated.
"Investors believed the stock had touched its bottom and were buying, expecting it to strengthen," a trader said.
Nigerian Breweries closed at 14.70 naira, up 20 kobo, after traders mopped its excess shares on the floor and appeared ready for more. Traders said this could end their woes for now.
The bullish trend persisted in the food/beverages, petroleum marketing, banking and conglomerate sectors, pushing prices higher, traders said.
Except for the slide of PZ Industries PZIN.LG, the conglomerates saw modest gains as Lever Brothers rose 30 kobo to 19.60 naira and UAC rose 25 kobo to 10.80 naira.

Cadbury kept on appreciating on its recent good results. It closed 35 kobo up at 32.05 naira. Nestle was 30 kobo up at 60.50 naira and Coca-Cola bottlers Nigerian Bottling Company finished at 42.00 naira, up 50 kobo.
Oil marketing shares strengthened. African Petroleum at 55.25 naira, Mobil at 60.00 naira, Texaco at 41.70 naira and National Oil at 57.10 naira, all added 20 kobo each.
Leading insurance firm AIICO remained attractive at 13.80 naira, up 30 kobo, followed by UNIC which closed 14 kobo higher at 4.60 naira.

Sustained appetite for bank shares saw the country's biggest four close higher. First Bank was 13.35 naira, up 35 kobo, UBA rose 20 kobo at 9.90 naira, Union Bank and Afribank were each 15 kobo higher, respectively, at 11.70 naira and 5.35 naira.

PZ, which enjoyed a brief respite in the past two days, resumed its slide on Wednesday, falling 20 kobo to 24.30 naira as investors dumped more of the stock for higher dividend-paying equities, according to one dealer.
